title: Filtered morphism restrictions to cycles, boundary quotients and representatives
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and U,V finite filtered integer-indexed cochain complexes [def-sp-filtration]. Fix p,q,r in Z with r >= 1, a filtered map t:U -> V, step restrictions s_i with their inclusion equations, and a graded map g with its quotient projection equation. Assume boundary-to-cycle containments hBZ for the subobjects [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. There exist kz:Z_r(U)->Z_r(V) and k:coker(B_r(U)->Z_r(U))->coker(B_r(V)->Z_r(V)) with the cycle inclusion and cokernel projection squares. The same g admits page-one restrictions kz₁,k₁ with those squares. There is also ρ:R_r(U)->R_r(V), restricting s_p in degree p+q to unquotiented cycle representatives, with its inclusion equation. All equations are exactly those of the Lean record. No comparison isomorphisms, homology naturality or image naturality are assumed or concluded.

source.place: Tag 012K, displayed cycle-boundary formulas and Lemma 12.24.4; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/012K

proof.text: The chain-map equation and filtration preservation imply s_p sends x with dx in F^(p+r) into the same condition in V. Apply the pullback universal property of complexCycleRepresentatives to restrict (s p).f(p+q), obtaining ρ and its inclusion equation.

The projection square for g sends the image of representatives defining complexCycles into the target cycle image, giving kz. The chain-map square preserves d(F^(p-r+1)), preservation of F^p preserves the intersection with that image, and preservation of F^(p+1) preserves the added filtration step. Projection therefore sends complexBoundaries into complexBoundaries. Restrict to the boundary subobjects, check the inclusion square by monic cancellation, then apply cokernel.map to get k.

Repeat the cycle and boundary restrictions at r=1 with the same s and g to get kz₁ and k₁. Zero objects and zero filtration steps obey the same universal properties, and r=1 needs no exceptional case.

proof_origin.place: Tag 012K, Lemma 12.24.4; categorical expansion of its explicit-representatives argument
